passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following section of this Form 10-K generally discusses 2025 and 2024 results and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussion of 2023 results and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in Part II, Item 7. “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 filed on February 25, 2025 . Description of Merck’s Business Merck & Co., Inc. (Merck or the Company) is a global health care company that delivers innovative health solutions through its prescription medicines, including biologic therapies, vaccines and animal health products. The Company’s operations are principally managed on a product basis and include two operating segments, Pharmaceutical and Animal Health, both of which are reportable segments. The Pharmaceutical segment includes human health pharmaceutical and vaccine products. Human health pharmaceutical products consist of therapeutic and preventive agents, generally sold by prescription, for the treatment of human disorders. The Company sells these human health pharmaceutical products primarily to drug wholesalers and retailers, hospitals, government agencies, and managed health care providers such as health maintenance organizations, pharmacy benefit managers and other institutions. Human health vaccine products consist of preventive pediatric, adolescent and adult vaccines. The Company sells these human health vaccines primarily to physicians, wholesalers, distributors and government entities. The Animal Health segment discovers, develops, manufactures and markets a wide range of veterinary pharmaceutical and vaccine products, as well as health management solutions and services, for the prevention, treatment and control of disease in all major livestock and companion animal species. The Company also offers an extensive suite of digitally connected identification, traceability and monitoring products. The Company sells its products to veterinarians, distributors, animal producers, farmers and pet owners. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The risks below are not the only ones the Company faces. Additional risks not currently known to the Company or that the Company presently deems immaterial may also impair its business operations. The Company’s business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows or prospects could be materially adversely affected by any of these risks. This Form 10-K also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. The Company’s results could materially differ from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of certain factors, including the risks it faces described below and elsewhere. See “Cautionary Factors that May Affect Future Results” below. Risks Related to the Company’s Business The Company is dependent on its patent rights, and if its patent rights are invalidated or circumvented, its business could be materially adversely affected. Patent protection is considered, in the aggregate, to be of material importance to the Company’s marketing of human health and animal health products in the U.S. and in most major foreign markets. Patents covering products that it has introduced normally provide market exclusivity, which is important for the successful marketing and sale of its products. The Company seeks patents covering each of its products in each of the markets where it intends to sell the products and where meaningful patent protection is available. Even if the Company succeeds in obtaining patents covering its products, third parties or government authorities may challenge or seek to invalidate or circumvent its patents and patent applications. It is important for the Company’s business to successfully assert and defend the patent rights that provide market exclusivity for its products. The Company is often involved in patent disputes relating to challenges to its patents or claims by third parties of infringement against the Company. The Company asserts and defends its patents both within and outside the U.S., including by filing claims of infringement against other parties. See Item 8. “Financial Statements and Supplementary Data,” Note 10. “Contingencies and Environmental Liabilities” below. In particular, manufacturers of generic or biosimilar pharmaceutical products from time to time file abbreviated NDAs or BLAs with the FDA seeking to market generic/biosimilar forms of the Company’s products prior to the expiration of relevant patents owned or licensed by the Company. The Company normally responds by asserting one or more of its patents with a lawsuit alleging patent infringement. Patent litigation and other challenges to the Company’s patents are costly and unpredictable and may deprive the Company of market exclusivity for a patented product or, in some cases, third-party patents may prevent the Company from marketing and selling a product in a particular geographic area. credit_strengths.text: Merck's operating margin sits well above the health care sector median, reflecting the pricing power of its patent-protected pharmaceutical and vaccine portfolio. This profitability, combined with modest leverage, underpins strong interest coverage that exceeds the sector median, providing a substantial cushion against earnings volatility from patent expirations or litigation.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure, generating free cash flow that represents a solid share of debt. This cash generation, alongside a current ratio above the sector median, supports liquidity and the ability to fund dividends, buybacks, and acquisitions without straining the balance sheet.

key_risks.text: Merck's reliance on patent-protected products exposes it to litigation and generic or biosimilar challenges that could erode market exclusivity. The risk-factor passage notes that patent disputes are costly and unpredictable, and that foreign governments may grant compulsory licenses, potentially reducing sales and cash flows from key products.

Debt increased sharply year over year, driven by acquisitions, and now includes meaningful maturities over the next several years. While near-term maturities are modest, the refinancing of these obligations and the funding of shareholder distributions and acquisitions will compete for cash flow, potentially limiting deleveraging if earnings decline.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally strong, with operating income covering interest expense many times over, well above the sector median. This provides ample capacity to service debt even if operating income were to decline significantly, and the company's leverage remains comfortably below the sector median.

Free cash flow to debt is solid, and operating cash flow covers capital expenditure with room to spare. However, dividends and buybacks absorb a substantial portion of free cash flow, leaving limited retained cash for debt reduction. Acquisitions further consume cash, so debt servicing relies on continued strong operating performance.

overall_credit_view.text: Merck's credit profile is supported by robust profitability, strong interest coverage, and leverage below the sector median. The indicative financial risk profile is modest, with net leverage well within the lower threshold tier. However, the sharp increase in debt from acquisitions and the potential for patent challenges warrant monitoring.

Looking forward, the company's ability to generate consistent free cash flow and manage patent expirations will be key to maintaining its credit strength. Shareholder distributions and acquisitions absorb most free cash flow, limiting deleveraging capacity. We view the credit as stable, but note that a sustained decline in operating cash flow or further debt-funded acquisitions could pressure the profile.

credit_strengths.text: 默克的經營利潤率遠高於醫療保健行業中位數，反映其受專利保護的藥品及疫苗組合的定價能力。此盈利能力結合適度的槓桿，支撐了超越行業中位數的強勁利息覆蓋率，為專利到期或訴訟帶來的盈利波動提供了厚實的緩衝。
經營現金流穩健地覆蓋資本開支，產生的自由現金流佔債務的比例可觀。此現金產生能力，加上高於行業中位數的流動比率，支持流動性以及在不對資產負債表造成壓力的情況下為股息、回購及收購提供資金的能力。

key_risks.text: 默克對專利保護產品的依賴使其面臨訴訟及學名藥或生物相似藥挑戰，可能侵蝕市場獨佔權。風險因素段落指出，專利糾紛成本高昂且難以預測，且外國政府可能授予強制許可，可能減少關鍵產品的銷售及現金流。
債務因收購而按年大幅增加，且現包括未來數年的重大到期債務。儘管近期到期債務規模不大，但這些債務的再融資以及股東分派和收購的資金需求將競爭現金流，若盈利下降，可能限制去槓桿。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率異常強勁，經營利潤覆蓋利息支出的倍數遠高於行業中位數。即使經營利潤大幅下降，這也提供了充足的償債能力，且公司的槓桿仍舒適地低於行業中位數。
自由現金流對債務的比率穩健，經營現金流覆蓋資本開支後仍有餘裕。然而，股息及回購吸收了自由現金流的很大部分，留下的留存現金有限，用於削減債務。收購進一步消耗現金，因此償債依賴於持續強勁的經營表現。

overall_credit_view.text: 默克的信用狀況受到強勁盈利能力、強勁利息覆蓋率及低於行業中位數的槓桿支持。指示性財務風險狀況為適度，淨槓桿遠低於較低門檻級別。然而，收購導致的債務大幅增加以及專利挑戰的可能性值得監察。
展望未來，公司產生持續自由現金流及管理專利到期的能力將是維持其信用實力的關鍵。股東分派及收購吸收了大部分自由現金流，限制了去槓桿能力。我們認為信用狀況穩定，但注意到經營現金流持續下降或進一步以債務融資的收購可能對其狀況構成壓力。
